mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate directly reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% indicates a tightening labor market, which typically precedes stronger corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE is below 4.5%, the 20-day forward return is negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous expansion in real GDP and housing starts (GDPC1 and HOUST) signal robust economic growth, which drives positive equity returns as corporate profits rise; the interaction effect is stronger than the sum of individual effects.
failure_condition: The interaction term (GDPC1 * HOUST) has a Rank IC below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window, or the combined signal fails to predict positive returns in 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), the Federal Reserve is likely to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as real rates rise and equity valuations contract.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0%, the 20-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates expanding manufacturing output, which correlates with stronger corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll growth rate exceeding 0.5% signals strong labor market conditions, which typically leads to higher consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5%, the 5-day forward return is negative in more than 45% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates broad-based consumer and business confidence, driving positive equity returns; the interaction effect is significant beyond the individual series.
failure_condition: The interaction term (RSAFS * HOUST) has a Rank IC below 0.01 over a 2-year rolling window, or the combined signal fails to predict positive returns in 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 2.0%), higher interest rates reduce corporate borrowing and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.0%, the 60-day forward return is positive in more than 45% of cases.
